data.name: Madan
data.gender_notes: Madan is used as a male name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root mad, 'to be intoxicated' — madana, 'cupid, passion'. Its root is Sanskrit mad (मद्). An epithet of Kama, the god of love. Madan is a Sanskrit name meaning “Intoxication; cupid; passion”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Madan expresses “Intoxication; cupid; passion”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit root mad, 'to be intoxicated' — madana, 'cupid, passion'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Madan total 15, reducing to 6. Number 6 is associated with responsibility, care and harmony.

vedic_reference.note: Madan is not a Vedic name, but it's derived from the Sanskrit word 'Madana' which means 'God of Love' and is mentioned in various Indian texts, including the Mahabharata.

historical_references.reference: An epithet of Kama, the god of love.
